findings.title: New sorted-set operations are incompatible with existing Redis segment keys
findings.body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created before this change are Redis sets, but process_spans now issues ZADD against them and the Lua script and _load_segment_data use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN. Redis will return WRONGTYPE for those keys, so batches for traces active during deployment can fail until the keys expire after redis_ttl (3600s), and mixed old/new consumers during rollout will break each other. No key-version bump, conversion, or fallback is provided.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate span scores instead of preserving timestamps
findings.body: Both merge sites call ZUNIONSTORE without an AGGREGATE clause, so Redis defaults to SUM. When the same payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets (e.g. duplicate delivery or a span stored under two keys before redirects converge), its score becomes roughly twice its end_timestamp_precise. That corrupts the ordering later used by ZPOPMIN eviction, causing duplicated spans to be retained while unrelated spans are evicted. The merge should use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) to preserve a real timestamp.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently flushes incomplete segments as if complete
findings.body: When a segment exceeds a hard-coded 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN discards the lowest end_timestamp_precise spans with no metric, log, or marker on the flushed segment. Those spans are permanently lost, yet flush_segments will emit the remainder as a normal segment (and the has-root flag/queue timeout may already have been set, so it flushes on the short root timeout). This replaces the previous explicit too-large-segment handling with silent partial data, ignores the configurable SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), and with tied scores eviction order is lexicographic by payload, so even a needed span can be dropped arbitrarily.

findings.title: Redirect chain resolution regresses from 10000 to 1000 hops
findings.body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations, removing the comment that explained the 10k limit. Segment trees whose parent chain needs more than 1000 redirect hops will stop at an intermediate span ID, so later spans are merged into the wrong set and the trace is flushed as multiple split segments instead of one segment. No test or justification covers chains between 1000 and 10000 hops.

findings.title: Flush-time max_segment_spans protection was removed without an equivalent guard
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer checks len(payloads[key]) against self.max_segment_spans, drops the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log, and returns arbitrarily large segments as long as they stay under the byte limit. Segments created before the Lua eviction existed, created by mixed-version workers, or built under a different configured limit will now be loaded and produced downstream regardless of the configured span cap, risking oversized Kafka messages and memory pressure during flush.

findings.title: process_batch now crashes the whole batch if end_timestamp_precise is absent
findings.body: Span construction changed from tolerating minimal span payloads to requiring val["end_timestamp_precise"] via direct indexing; the cast to SpanEvent is typing-only and does not validate the runtime JSON. A single older or malformed message missing that field raises KeyError, aborting process_batch for every span in the batch and causing the same batch to be retried instead of only the bad message being dropped or defaulted.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime-ordered audit log endpoint
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders AuditLogEntry by -datetime, so the value is a datetime: build_cursor will raise TypeError from math.floor(datetime) on any non-empty first page, and on later pages build_queryset would compare a datetime column against a raw integer timestamp instead of the datetime conversion DateTimePaginator performs. The optimized audit-log path therefore returns 500 instead of results.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination crashes Django querysets despite claiming ORM support
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and a caller supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers), get_result slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it; stop can also become <= 0 for sufficiently negative offsets. A privileged audit-log user can thus force a 500 with a crafted cursor, and BasePaginator's similar change at the shared get_result only clamps non-prev cursors, leaving prev cursors unclamped.

findings.title: No tests cover eviction, score merging, or the new paginator path
findings.body: The added/updated tests only supply end_timestamp_precise for existing small-segment scenarios. Nothing inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify how many and which spans survive ZPOPMIN, whether the root span is retained, or how duplicate payloads merged by ZUNIONSTORE keep their scores, and there are no tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator against a datetime-ordered queryset or for negative cursors. The riskiest new behaviors in this change are therefore unverified.
